newsitem.title: singapore: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil firm on fresh demand.
newsitem.headline: Asia Gas Oil/Jet - Gas oil firm on fresh demand.

text.p: Singapore gas oil firmed on Wednesday on fresh buying support from several traders despite a flood of offers, traders said.
Traders said the bulk of the eight offers were above $25.50 per barrel with those below this price receiving ample buying interest.
The market was well bid at just over the $25.00 mark with two 150,000-barrel cargoes traded at above this mark.
A European refiner sold to a local trader one cargo at $25.25 per barrel for June 2-6 lifting, and another European trader sold to a Japanese trader at $25.20 for May 22-26 lifting, they said.

Traders said the renewed buying interest was in part due to the buyers' expectations that there is enduser demand for gas oil at these levels, especially from China where sales were done at just under $200 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis.
Firmer prices were also attributed to strong crude prices June Brent last traded up 13 cents to $18.17 per barrel on top of a 10 cent overnight gain.
Reflective of the fresh demand, the swaps market also rose with May last quoted up 15 cents from Tuesday at $25.10/$25.20 per barrel, brokers said.

May swaps traded to an intra-day high of $25.45 before easing to trade at $24.30, they said. The May/June spread is narrowing in line with the flat physical market with the backwardation now valued at about 40 cents with 50 cents traded earlier in the day.
Taiwan issued a tender to sell 225,000-250,000 barrels of gas oil for June 14-17 lifting. The tender closes on May 13.

The jet fuel market also received renewed support with a local trader buying two 100,000-barrel cargoes from a European major at $25.00 for May 22-26 lifting and at $25.30 for June 2-6 lifting, traders said.
Jet fuel traded on Tuesday at $25.00.
